articles.title: ‘Anti-India Ravana’ Posters Featuring Akhilesh Yadav, Rahul Gandhi, Elon Musk Surface In Lucknow
articles.description: Posters titled ‘Anti-India Dashanan Ravana’ have become a talking point in Lucknow after appearing at several intersections across the city. The posters feature the faces of former MP Atiq Ahmed, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and American businessman Elon Musk, among others. They are reportedly the work of the Sanatan Raksha Sangathan. The posters depict 10 individuals as the different heads of Ravana. Apart from Atiq Ahmed, Akhilesh Yadav, Rahul Gandhi and Elon Musk, the faces include US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, Bangladesh's Muhammad Yunus, George Soros, Prashant Bhushan and Mukhtar Ansari. Through the posters, the organisation has accused these individuals of engaging in activities against India and attempting to destabilise the country. Sanatan Raksha Sangathan Levels Serious Allegations The Sanatan Raksha Sangathan has alleged that some of the individuals featured in the posters have been associated with attempts to destabilise India's political and social systems. The organisation has referred to Elon Musk's social media posts, alleged anti-India remarks by Ilhan Omar and her visit to Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). It has also cited Muhammad Yunus's role following the change of power in Bangladesh and alleged objectionable remarks concerning India's northeastern states. George Soros has been accused of attempting to destabilise India. Akhilesh Yadav, Prashant Bhushan Also Targeted The posters also target Akhilesh Yadav and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan. The organisation alleges that Yadav has shared a platform with people who have spoken about a coup in India. Prashant Bhushan has also been accused of making statements publicly advocating a coup, according to the organisation. The posters have drawn attention at several intersections in Lucknow, triggering discussion in the city. However, the allegations levelled against the individuals featured in them are claims made by the organisation and have not been independently verified.

articles.title: Escalation In Middle East As Iran Hits Kurdish Bases In Erbil; Blast Hits Iraqi Militia HQ
articles.description: Iran has reportedly launched another drone strike against an Iranian Kurdish opposition group based in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region. Drones targeted a Komala Party base in Balisan, Erbil province, damaging buildings but causing no reported casualties. The attack follows a separate drone strike on a camp belonging to the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDPI) in Koya district. Since the US-Israeli war against Iran began on February 28, more than 1,000 drones and missiles have reportedly targeted the Kurdistan Region, launched by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Iran-backed Iraqi militias. Meanwhile, clashes between Iranian forces and Kurdish fighters have intensified in western Iran, adding to regional tensions as Tehran faces mounting military and security pressures.

articles.title: Peace only way for Manipur to participate in India''s development journey: CM
articles.description: Imphal, Oct 17 (PTI): Manipur Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh on Saturday said peace is the only way for the ethnic strife-torn state to participate in the country's journey of development. His comment came on a day when a man was shot dead and four others were injured in a gun attack by suspected militants in Kamjong district. Addressing a programme - Jan Sevak Mahakumbh - here, the chief minister said India cannot be considered a developed country without the development of Manipur. "Peace is the only way for the state to participate in the journey of development," he said. The ethnic conflict that erupted in May 2023 between the Imphal valley-based Meitei and hill-based Kuki communities has claimed at least 306 lives, while 49 people remain missing and thousands have been left homeless. In recent months, clashes between Kuki and Naga communities have also been reported. State Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam stated that restoring peace in Manipur requires mutual trust and understanding among all communities. Addressing the Jan Sevak Mahakumbh here, the chief minister said the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' has been observed across all districts of Manipur from September 17 to October 17 to mark the 25 years of public service rendered by Narendra Modi as Gujarat chief minister and then as the prime minister. "The successful month-long campaign witnessed the participation of more than 4 lakh people in 6,122 venues across the state," Singh added. The CM said the Manipuri language serves as a medium of communication among all communities in the state and emphasised the need to cherish the language and encourage its wider use among the people. Under the leadership of the prime minister, the vision of 'Viksit Bharat' 2047 is to build a strong India by the time the country attains 100 years of independence, he said. Referring to the public demand for the updation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC) before the Census, Singh said the Centre has been informed about the concerns raised by the people of Manipur and has deferred the Census exercise in the state.
